note: Out-of-bounds read: accesses y->p[1] without checking y->sz >= 2. When y->sz == 1, this reads past the allocated limb array.
Creates bigint with sz == 1 when the value fits in one limb. This is the vulnerable state that triggers the OOB read in mpz_get_int.
bint_norm calls mpz_get_int on newly created bigints. If the bigint has sz == 1, this triggers the OOB read.
mrb_bint_cmp calls mpz_get_int when comparing a bigint with an integer. If the bigint has sz == 1, this triggers the OOB read.

mrb_bint_mul_ii creates bigints from integers via mpz_init_set_int, multiplies them, then calls bint_norm which invokes mpz_get_int. If the multiplication result fits in one limb (sz == 1), the OOB read occurs.
mrb_div_int_value calls mrb_bint_mul_ii when MRB_INT_MIN / -1 overflows. This is one entry point to reach the vulnerable code path.
mpz_init_set_str parses string representations of big integers. If the string represents a small value, the resulting bigint has sz == 1.
Loading IREP_TT_BIGINT constants from bytecode calls mrb_bint_new_str, which can create a sz == 1 bigint if the string represents a small value.
new_litbn stores big integer literals as strings in the pool. The compiler uses IREP_TT_BIGINT for integer literals that overflow mrb_int.

code: int off = new_litbn(s, p, base, FALSE); genop_2(s, OP_LOADL, cursp(), off);
note: NODE_INT case: when readint reports overflow, the compiler creates a bigint literal via new_litbn and emits OP_LOADL.

code: int off = new_litbn(s, p, base, TRUE); genop_2(s, OP_LOADL, cursp(), off);
note: NODE_NEGATE case: negative big integer literals that overflow mrb_int are also stored as IREP_TT_BIGINT constants.
String-to-integer conversion calls mrb_bint_new_str when the value overflows mrb_int. The string is parsed by mpz_init_set_str.
The condition evaluates y->p[1] even when digits(y) == 1 due to short-circuit evaluation. When y->sz == 1, this is an out-of-bounds read.
The vulnerable line reads y->p[1] without checking y->sz >= 2. For a sz == 1 bigint, this reads past the allocated limb array, causing a heap-buffer-overflow.

code: if (mpz_get_int(&b->mp, &i1)) { if (i1 == i2) return 0; if (i1 > i2) return 1; return -1; }
note: When comparing a bigint with sz == 1 against an integer, mpz_get_int performs the OOB read. This is the primary trigger path for the vulnerability.
